procedural.statement: The salt bridge S1 argues from is load-bearing: mutating D17 to alanine drops the predicted melting point to 71.4 C, below the objective's threshold.

procedural.provenance: Three runs on the claimant's node after a validator found S1 insufficient. Seeds 0 to 2, spread 0.9 C.

body.detail: A validator passed the salt-bridge item as holding but found it insufficient to establish that the bridge is what stabilises the fold. It was right: S1 was an argument with nothing under it. This adds the knockout that tests it. The claim itself is untouched and its hash is unchanged.

items.note: Derived the melting point myself from the deposited coordinates and reached 81.1 C. Under this mode the leader settled relevance when it wrote the procedure, so the second question is not mine to weigh.
Ran the five folds. Spread 1.4 C against the claimant's 1.3, and the minimum stays above the threshold.
The salt bridge is there. Whether it is the interaction doing the stabilising is an argument the claim does not carry evidence for, and I cannot settle it by reading.

spans.quote: tm_celsius = 81.1, from the objective's stated procedure over the deposited coordinates.

predicates.reason: Folded it myself and reached the same structure; it is a binder against the named target.
The claim supplies the input and the procedure derived the measurement, which is what this mode requires. I derived it independently and matched.

spans.quote: the stabilising contact is a buried salt bridge between the binder's D17 and the target's R204

predicates.reason: The bridge is there. That it is what stabilises the fold is asserted rather than shown, and nothing in the claim tests it — a knockout would.
Compared against every admitted claim in this objective; no shared topology.

body.rationale: Reproduced the fold independently rather than inspecting the claimant's artifact, so this is a second observation and not a second opinion about the first one. The semantic item is the weak part: it is plausible and it is not established, which is why that one item reads insufficient while the claim as a whole passes on the deterministic evidence the mode makes authoritative.

envelopes.name: signed by another key

body.significance: A binder against TR-9 with a predicted melting point of 81.1 C, which clears the objective's 75 C threshold by six degrees and does so on a backbone topology no admitted claim uses.

deterministic.statement: tm_celsius = 81.1, from the objective's stated procedure over the deposited coordinates.
deterministic.provenance: ColabFold 1.5.5 against UniRef90 2026_01, seed 0, run on the claimant's node. The objective's procedure derives the measurement; this supplies its input.

deterministic.statement: binding_kcal = -10.4, below the -9.0 the criteria require.
deterministic.provenance: Same structure, scored with the tool and version the criteria name.

procedural.statement: The melting point holds across five independent folds of the same sequence, so the figure is not an artefact of one seed.

procedure.statement: Fold the sequence five times with different seeds and take the spread of the predicted melting points.
inputs: the sequence in the claim's assertion

procedural.provenance: Five runs on the claimant's node, seeds 0 to 4. Spread was 1.3 C.

semantic.statement: The stabilising contact is a buried salt bridge between the binder's D17 and the target's R204, which is the interaction the objective's criteria describe as the one worth finding.
semantic.provenance: Read off the deposited coordinates by the claimant. An argument, offered to be judged rather than checked.

references: Jumper et al. 2021, Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold, Nature 596
